title: Bad Trips Guide, Round 15
intro: Round 15 (2026-11-07). Round 14 is in. Three cards: one line in Who to Contact's first list, one lead-in in For the Person Helping, and the "real grief" paragraph cut as a repeat. That cut is yours to decide rather than mine, because the safety check tracks two of its warnings (dragging someone out of grief, trapping them in a loop). Round 12's card is still open on its own page.

suggestions.title: The stay-present phrase, its lead-in said to the sitter
suggestions.reading: After the Human first half, the paragraph as the guide has it reads [60%](https://www.pangram.com/history/94e4bf77-43c1-445b-b9f2-cf75d80fb451).
suggestions.tested: With this change: [45%](https://www.pangram.com/history/2410f074-0033-4869-8dac-a1949eb371d3), the phrase's lines Human. The phrase itself is unchanged.
suggestions.what: "A useful phrase is:" becomes "If it helps, you can say to yourself:".
suggestions.why: The readers flagged "A useful phrase is:" as advice-article scaffolding. Saying who says the phrase (the sitter, to themselves) is plainer and makes clear it's for steadying the helper.
suggestions.stays: "Stay present.", both phrases word for word, and their italics.
suggestions.deciding: Approve puts the new lead-in in; Revise lets you change it first.
suggestions.advice_note: Approve: the same phrase, and the paragraph reads better with it.

edits.before: Stay present. A useful phrase is: This feeling is allowed to move through. I don't have to become it. I can love the part of me that feels it. Or simply: Can I send love to the one who's suffering?
edits.after: Stay present. If it helps, you can say to yourself: This feeling is allowed to move through. I don't have to become it. I can love the part of me that feels it. Or simply: Can I send love to the one who's suffering?

suggestions.title: The "real grief" paragraph, said already
suggestions.reading: After the Human first half, the paragraph by itself reads [AI, 100%](https://www.pangram.com/history/763fcc5d-16e6-42d3-be3f-47f0dd2b9a04), and all three readers flagged all three of its sentences. Rewording it read AI too (the quip cut, [100%](https://www.pangram.com/history/e31e6cea-2eb3-4f5a-9e7c-3dad46058085); the two don'ts joined, [83%](https://www.pangram.com/history/959f47f9-1338-4ccd-bede-0ce54ce78326)).
suggestions.tested: The opening without it, after the Human first half: [79%](https://www.pangram.com/history/0fe50afc-728a-4281-ab3b-5d3df305842c). The opening's other paragraphs still read AI; this card takes out the part that only repeats.
suggestions.what: "Don't drag somebody out of real grief. Don't trap them inside a loop that is grinding them down either. Love isn't stubbornness." goes.
suggestions.why: "Don't drag somebody out of real grief" is the paragraph two above ("Crying, grieving, remembering, or touching a genuine wound calls for loving awareness."). Not leaving them stuck in a grinding loop is what The Fear/Panic Loop section is for. The last line is a quip. It's your call rather than mine because the safety check tracks two of its warnings, dragging someone out of grief and trapping them in a loop; with the cut they live in those two places.
suggestions.stays: The grief paragraph above it, "Stay present." and its phrase, and The Fear/Panic Loop section.
suggestions.deciding: Approve cuts the paragraph; Reject keeps it.
suggestions.advice_note: Approve: both points are already made where a reader needs them.
suggestions.found_by: the say-it-once look across the guide, stopped by the fidelity check (it holds two warnings)

edits.before: Don't drag somebody out of real grief. Don't trap them inside a loop that is grinding them down either. Love isn't stubbornness.
